newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins steady, consolidate after rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins steady, consolidate after rise.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds were steady in calm trade on Tuesday after Monday's rise and dealers said prices were consolidating at new levels amid profit-taking.

"There is paper on the market people want to get rid of. The trend is not obvious and it is difficult to say where the market would go in the absence of news or U.S. figures," an Aljba Alliance Bank dealer said.
MinFins, like other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news which would suggest a change in U.S. interest rates and consequently affect U.S. Treasury bond prices.
Dealers said the most active trading was seen in the fourth tranche on the narrow market, with Russian banks mainly on the offer side and Western banks buying, apparently on client demand.
They added prices of tranches from 3 to 7 were meeting resistance this week at 89.60, 65.65, 46.75, 52.75 and 40.50 respectively.
